question: If $f(x) = \sin(x) + |x|$, check continuity at $x=0$.
explanation:
Left-hand limit:

$\lim_{x \to 0^-} (\sin x + |x|) = 0$.

Right-hand limit:

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} (\sin x + |x|) = 0$.

$f(0)=0$.

Since LHL = RHL = $f(0)$, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$.

options.A: $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$ because LHL = RHL = $f(0)=0$
options.B: $f(x)$ is discontinuous at $x=0$ because $|x|$ is not continuous at $0$
options.C: $f(x)$ is discontinuous at $x=0$ because LHL $\neq$ RHL
